knowledge_learned: Every nonnegative power of ten has remainder one modulo 3 and modulo 9. Thus a decimal integer and its digit sum have the same remainder for either divisor.
Reordering the digits preserves that remainder. A repunit with k ones has the same remainder as k, so nine ones form the shortest repunit divisible by nine.
Splitting a decimal integer into contiguous chunks and adding their values also preserves the remainder modulo 3 or 9, because each chunk has the same remainder as its own digit sum.
mechanics_observed: A visual grouping example motivates a remainder prediction.
Short checked questions alternate with worked explanations and optional Why feedback.
Exercises move from individual numbers to digit permutations, repeated-digit patterns, and a general claim about splitting numbers into chunks.
